picks.why: Erbusco house of 1968, exacting and given to long lees ageing; its Riserva, named for the founder's mother, is the prestige cuvée of Franciacorta the library already teaches.
picks.note: The library also holds the wine as w-annamaria-clementi; confirm the label's word order (Franciacorta Riserva Annamaria Clementi) and give the founder's mother her dates only from two sources, else describe her.

picks.why: Erbusco house of 1977 with barrel fermented base wines; its vintage Satèn, Chardonnay alone at lower pressure, teaches the style whose name the Franciacorta consorzio coined.
picks.note: The house's prestige Riserva carries its living founder's name, so the Satèn is taught. The library writes Franciacorta Gran Cuvée Satèn, an older name: confirm the label for the years taught (now a vintage Franciacorta Satèn) and that it is Chardonnay alone.

picks.why: Chiuro house of 1897 with its cellar in the castle there, long the valley's largest; 5 Stelle is the dried grape Nebbiolo the library teaches Sforzato di Valtellina with.
picks.note: The library writes Sfursat di Valtellina 5 Stelle and the region record 5 Stelle Sfursat: confirm the label's word order and its DOCG.

picks.why: Sondrio family house of the Valtellina terraces, with long macerations, large old casks and late release; Rocce Rosse is its Valtellina Superiore Sassella Riserva.
picks.note: Confirm the Riserva is still made as Rocce Rosse and how long it is held before release; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Sirmione family estate on the south shore of Lake Garda, there since 1939 by its own account; I Frati is its Lugana of Turbiana, the white side of the region.
picks.note: Confirm 1939 from a second source, the label (Lugana I Frati) and its grapes; Brolettino is the house's oak aged Lugana for the others.

picks.why: Montefalco estate of 1971 that made dry Sagrantino a modern wine through clonal work with the University of Milan; 25 Anni is the bottling that carried Sagrantino abroad.
picks.note: Confirm 25 Anni's first vintage and what its name marks before telling either.

picks.why: Small Montefalco family estate of long macerations, no additions and late release; Pagliaro is its single vineyard Montefalco Sagrantino, the natural wine reference of the zone.
picks.note: The house keeps its name; name no living member of the family in prose, and confirm the label (Montefalco Sagrantino Pagliaro).

picks.why: The Torgiano house that won the village a DOC in 1968 and its Rosso Riserva a DOCG in 1990; Rubesco Riserva Vigna Monticchio is the wine of that DOCG.
picks.note: The library writes Rubesco Vigna Monticchio Riserva and the region record Rubesco Riserva Vigna Monticchio: confirm the label's order and the founder's dates before naming him.

picks.why: The Antinori family's Orvieto castle estate, with its own label; Cervaro della Sala, Chardonnay with Grechetto fermented in barrique, is the Umbrian white a sommelier meets.
picks.note: Wave one holds Marchesi Antinori in Chianti Classico with Tignanello; this is the family's Umbrian estate, its own home and a different wine. Confirm its purchase by the family (1940 by its account) and Cervaro's first vintage.

picks.why: Organic family estate above Lake Corbara in the Orvieto Classico zone; Calcaia is its sweet Orvieto of noble rot, the style the lake's autumn mists allow.
picks.note: Sources give 1981 or 1986 for Calcaia's first vintage: confirm, and confirm the label's words (Orvieto Classico Superiore Muffa Nobile Calcaia).

picks.why: Loreto Aprutino estate of old pergola vines that bottles only in the years it accepts; its Trebbiano d'Abruzzo is the white the library teaches as proof the grape can age.
picks.note: The library also holds the wine as w-trebbiano-valentini; build on both, and name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Torano Nuovo house of 1964 in the Teramo hills, unfiltered and long held in bottle, its old vintages decanted by hand before release; its Montepulciano d'Abruzzo is the flagship.
picks.note: The house keeps its founder's name; confirm whether he is living before giving dates, and name no living member of the family.

picks.why: San Martino sulla Marrucina house of 1981 that took polished, oak aged Montepulciano d'Abruzzo abroad; Villa Gemma Riserva is its flagship and the modern pole of the region.
picks.note: Confirm the label (Montepulciano d'Abruzzo Riserva Villa Gemma) and the founder's dates from two sources before naming him.

picks.why: Controguerra house of 1890 in the Teramo hills and a founder of the Colline Teramane DOCG; Zanna is its long aged Montepulciano Riserva.
picks.note: Confirm 1890, Zanna's label (Montepulciano d'Abruzzo Colline Teramane Riserva) and its first vintage from the house and a second source.

picks.why: Ofena estate in the hot basin under the Gran Sasso; Piè delle Vigne, Montepulciano made pink, is its Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo, the region's deep coloured rosato.
picks.note: One source names the Montepulciano Tonì the house's flagship; the Cerasuolo is chosen so the group holds the rosato. Confirm with the house, and confirm the label (Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo, Superiore or not).

picks.why: Manduria estate of 2004 working old alberello Primitivo vines; Es is the Primitivo di Manduria that argued the appellation could be fine as well as big.
picks.note: The house carries its living founder's name: the house may be named, the person never in prose.

picks.why: Castel del Monte house of 1950 that championed Nero di Troia; Il Falcone, Nero di Troia with Montepulciano, is the Riserva that carried the grape and the DOCG of 2011.
picks.note: Confirm the house's seat at Andria and the label (Castel del Monte Rosso Riserva Il Falcone) for the years taught.

picks.why: Salice Salentino house dating its origins to 1665; Five Roses, a Negroamaro rosato of the Salento bottled from 1943, is the one the house tells as the first rosato bottled in Italy.
picks.note: Confirm 1665 and 1943 from the house and a second source, and hedge the first bottled rosato as the house's claim.

picks.why: Guagnano estate of the Salento whose founder died in 1999; Patriglione, Negroamaro partly dried on the vine, began as a forgotten cask of the 1970s and became the house's flagship.
picks.note: Sources give 1974 or 1975 for the first Patriglione: confirm, and give Cosimo Taurino his birth year only from two sources.

picks.why: Estate between Acquaviva delle Fonti and Gioia del Colle with a cellar dug into the limestone; its numbered Gioia del Colle Primitivo shows the fresher side of the grape on the Murge.
picks.note: A thin pick: confirm which numbered bottling (16 or 17) the house leads with, what the number means and the label's exact words (the plan's words must stand in it); Cantine San Marzano's Sessantanni is the alternative if neither stands.

picks.why: Serdiana estate of 1938; Turriga, a Cannonau led barrique blend first made in 1988, is the Sardinian red a candidate is expected to name.
picks.note: Confirm the first vintage of 1988, the blend and the label's appellation (Isola dei Nuraghi IGT).

picks.why: Alghero estate founded in 1899 by two Piedmontese on reclaimed land, first as a nursery of rootstocks; Terre Bianche is its Torbato, a grape the house long grew almost alone.
picks.note: Confirm Terre Bianche against its selection Cuvée 161 as the bottling to teach, and the Torbato claim; Anghelu Ruju and Marchese di Villamarina are the others.

picks.why: Cabras family house of 1898 on the Oristano gulf; Antico Gregori, blended from very old reserves, is the Vernaccia di Oristano the library teaches, aged under flor in the Sherry manner.
picks.note: Confirm how Antico Gregori is blended and labelled (it may carry no vintage).

picks.why: The Sulcis co-operative and the voice of its zone; Terre Brune, first made in 1984, turned old ungrafted Carignano on sand into a serious Carignano del Sulcis Superiore.
picks.note: Confirm the first vintage of 1984 and the grapes beside Carignano (Bovaleddu, as the library says).

picks.why: Arzachena estate in the granite of the Gallura that made Vermentino a wine of weight and ageing, long labelled outside the DOCG; its late picked, dry Vendemmia Tardiva is the wine the library names first.
picks.note: Confirm the Vendemmia Tardiva against the estate's Capichera Classico as the flagship, and the appellation its label carries in the years taught.

picks.why: Modena house of 1860 and a reference for dry Lambrusco; Vecchia Modena Premium is its pale, sharp Lambrusco di Sorbara, the side of the family the library sets against Grasparossa.
picks.note: Confirm the label (Lambrusco di Sorbara Vecchia Modena Premium) and how it is made, in tank or in bottle.

picks.why: Reggio Emilia family house whose dry Concerto, a Reggiano Lambrusco, helped restore the name of dry Lambrusco on the Reggio side.
picks.note: Confirm the house's founding, Concerto's grape and first vintage, and any claim of a first before telling it.

picks.why: Sorbara family estate of 1926 in the Cristo di Sorbara; Radice is its pale Lambrusco di Sorbara refermented in bottle and left on its lees, the old way of the zone.
picks.note: Confirm 1926 from a second source; Leclisse, from the oldest vines and made in tank, is the house's other Sorbara.

picks.why: Faenza estate whose Scacco Matto, a botrytised Albana passito, makes the case for Albana di Romagna, the first white DOCG of Italy in 1987.
picks.note: Confirm the estate's founding and Scacco Matto's first vintage and label (Romagna Albana Passito).

picks.why: Historic estate of the Colli Piacentini; Ageno, Malvasia di Candia with Ortrugo and Trebbiano fermented long on its skins, is the house's flagship and the orange wine of the region.
picks.note: Unchecked this run: confirm the estate's village (Rivergaro), its founding and the founder the wine is named for, with dates, and Ageno's blend and appellation (Emilia IGT).

picks.why: Castelli di Jesi family estate whose Villa Bucci Riserva, matured in large old casks, makes the case for Verdicchio as a white to age.
picks.note: Confirm the appellation on the label (Castelli di Jesi Verdicchio Riserva Classico, a DOCG) for the years taught.

picks.why: Matelica estate in the landlocked upper valley; Mirum is its Verdicchio di Matelica Riserva, the tighter, slower inland Verdicchio the library sets against Jesi.
picks.note: Confirm Mirum's grapes (Verdicchio, perhaps with a little Chardonnay in some years) and its first vintage.

picks.why: Castelplanio house whose amphora shaped bottle, chosen by a design competition of 1953, carried Verdicchio abroad; Titulus is the Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi Classico that wears it.
picks.note: Confirm the competition of 1953 and the move to Castelplanio in 1956 with a second source; tell the house's owners only as history with years.

picks.why: Osimo house of the Conero and the Castelli di Jesi; Cùmaro, Montepulciano from the slopes of Monte Conero, is its Conero Riserva, the red side of the Marche.
picks.note: Unchecked this run: confirm the house's seat at Osimo and its founding, Cùmaro's appellation (Conero Riserva DOCG) and its first vintage.

picks.why: Ascoli Piceno house of the southern Marche, known for the Piceno reds and the Offida whites; Roggio del Filare, Montepulciano with Sangiovese, is its Rosso Piceno Superiore.
picks.note: Unchecked this run: confirm the house's founding, Roggio del Filare's blend and appellation; its Offida Pecorino is the white alternative.

picks.why: Growers' co-operative at Groppo above Manarola and the voice of the cliffs, gathering grapes from many small terraces; its Cinque Terre Sciacchetrà is the sweet wine of dried Bosco, Albarola and Vermentino.
picks.note: Unchecked this run: confirm the co-operative's founding, its name as it writes it and the Sciacchetrà's label and grapes.

picks.why: Dolceacqua estate whose Rossese vines go back to 1870 by the family's account; Bricco Arcagna, from the top of the Arcagna hill, is its Rossese di Dolceacqua.
picks.note: Confirm 1870 with a second source, and whether the label reads Rossese di Dolceacqua or Dolceacqua, Superiore or not.

picks.why: Family house of the Colli di Luni on the Tuscan border, named for the Roman city of Luni; Etichetta Nera is its fuller Vermentino, given skin contact and a longer time on its lees.
picks.note: Confirm the house's founding and how it writes its name (Cantine Lunae Bosoni); the label reads Colli di Luni Vermentino Etichetta Nera.

picks.why: Aymavilles estate founded in 1989 by a family long rooted in the valley; Cuvée Bois, a barrel fermented Chardonnay, is its flagship, with Petite Arvine and Fumin for the native grapes.
picks.note: Confirm 1989 and Cuvée Bois as the flagship; Petite Arvine is the native alternative if the house leads with it. Name no living member of the family.

picks.producer: Cave Mont Blanc de Morgex et La Salle
picks.wine: Blanc de Morgex et de La Salle
picks.why: The co-operative of 1983 under Mont Blanc and the voice of its appellation, making Blanc de Morgex et de La Salle from ungrafted Prié Blanc grown at up to about 1,200 metres.
picks.note: Confirm the bottling to teach (the still DOC white, or a named cuvée such as Rayon) and the house's name as it writes it.

picks.why: Monte Porzio Catone house whose wines carried Frascati abroad; Vigneto Santa Teresa, a single vineyard on the volcanic hills, is its Frascati Superiore.
picks.note: Confirm the vineyard's first vintage and its blend of Malvasia and Trebbiano; Luna Mater Riserva is the house's other Frascati Superiore.

picks.why: Grottaferrata estate whose first wines of 1993 followed years of replanting with the University of Milan; Vigna Adriana, Malvasia del Lazio with Viognier, is its white, sold outside the Frascati DOCG.
picks.note: Sources differ on the dates of the research and the cellar (1985 or 1992): confirm, and confirm Vigna Adriana's appellation (Lazio IGT).

picks.why: Montefiascone house of the Est! Est!! Est!!! country; Montiano, a Merlot sold as a Lazio IGT, is the red that drew notice to the north of the region.
picks.note: Unchecked this run: confirm the house's founding, Montiano's first vintage and appellation. Its founders are living (one is on people.json): name nobody.

picks.why: Acuto family estate of the Cesanese del Piglio, with roots it dates to 1921; Torre del Piano is its Cesanese del Piglio Superiore Riserva, from the red DOCG of Lazio.
picks.note: Confirm 1921 and Torre del Piano's vineyard and ageing with the house and a second source.

picks.why: Le Ferriere estate of 1967 on the reclaimed Agro Pontino, known for trials of many grapes and for reviving Bellone; Mater Matuta, Syrah with Petit Verdot, is its red, named for the goddess of a sanctuary found on the estate.
picks.note: Confirm 1967, the blend and the sanctuary's site; Anthium, its Bellone, is the native alternative.

picks.why: Barile house of 1925 with cellars cut into the volcanic tuff, a historic name of traditional, long aged Aglianico del Vulture; Don Anselmo is its classic bottling.
picks.note: Confirm Don Anselmo's appellation (Aglianico del Vulture Superiore DOCG or the DOC) for the years taught, and any later change of ownership as history with its year.

picks.why: Barile estate of 2000 on the slopes of Monte Vulture whose single high vineyard gives Titolo, the Aglianico del Vulture the library sets against Taurasi.
picks.note: The house carries its living founder's name: the house may be named, the person never in prose. Confirm the vineyard's place (Contrada Solagna del Titolo).

picks.why: Rionero in Vulture house with cellars in tuff caves of the seventeenth century, whose wines take notarial names; La Firma, from late picked Aglianico, is its Aglianico del Vulture.
picks.note: Confirm the house's founding and La Firma's appellation (the DOC, or the Superiore DOCG in some years).

picks.why: Cirò Marina family house and a reference for Cirò and for the revival of Calabria's native grapes; Duca Sanfelice is its Cirò Rosso Classico Superiore Riserva of Gaglioppo.
picks.note: Gravello, Gaglioppo with Cabernet Sauvignon, is called the house's flagship by some; Duca Sanfelice is chosen to teach Cirò. Confirm the label's spelling (Sanfelice or San Felice).

picks.why: Family estate of the Ionian coast by Bianco, run over three generations, making the passito Greco di Bianco, a DOC reserved for sweet wine of dried grapes.
picks.note: A thin pick: confirm the estate's village (Casignana or Caraffa del Bianco), its founding and the bottling taught (the white label or the black).
